Implemented request validation rejecting null `title`, `email`, `is_active`, and `is_superuser` with 422. Omitted fields remain supported; `description` and `full_name` remain clearable. Public response models are unchanged.

Added regression tests for rejection, unchanged persisted data, and clearing nullable fields.

Syntax and diff checks passed. Route tests remain unverified: `uv` crashed, and direct pytest lacked `sqlmodel`.

staging 전용 설정을 준비했습니다.

- `compose.deploy.yml`: 이미지와 worker 수를 환경변수로 지정하도록 변경
- `.env.staging`: `ENVIRONMENT=staging` 추가
- 기존 `.env`와 prod 기본값(`backend:latest`, worker 4개) 유지
- Compose 설정 검증 완료. 실제 배포는 실행하지 않았습니다.

수정했습니다.

- `read_items()`의 count와 목록을 단일 SQL로 조회합니다. 빈 페이지에서도 전체 count를 유지합니다.
- `(owner_id, created_at)` 복합 인덱스를 모델과 Alembic 마이그레이션에 추가했습니다. downgrade도 지원합니다.
- 권한별 조회와 페이지 경계 조건 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다.

구문 검사와 `git diff --check`는 통과했습니다. 테스트 실행은 `sqlmodel` 미설치와 `uv` 내부 오류로 완료하지 못했습니다. DB 마이그레이션은 아직 적용하지 않았습니다.

Added [CI workflow](.github/workflows/ci.yml) because this checkout had none.

- Caches `.next/cache` using lockfile and source hashes.
- Restores via a lockfile-only prefix when source changes.
- Runs caching before the build.

Validated YAML and step ordering. Actual cache restoration needs a CI run.

Implemented the importer, partner mappings, timezone CSV, provenance migration, sample drop, and regression tests.

Loads replace the date’s imported rows transactionally and validate manifest counts. Sample setup requires an existing `admin@example.com` user; instructions are in `backend/app/importers/README.md`.

Syntax and diff checks passed. Runtime acceptance remains unverified: `uv` crashes in macOS system configuration, and the available Python lacks dependencies.

Implemented a minimal three-file change with all signatures unchanged:

- Access tokens carry `"type": "access"`.
- Reset tokens carry `"type": "password_reset"`.
- Both validators reject wrong or missing types before subject lookup.

Isolated checks passed for valid tokens, cross-use rejection, missing types, and expiration. Full backend tests were blocked by missing `sqlmodel`.

Previously issued tokens without a type claim are now rejected.

Added `--dry-run`, threaded through `main()` → `init()` → `init_db()`. It prints email, `is_superuser`, and status (`already exists` / `would be created`), then returns before user creation.

Verified CLI propagation and existing/missing-user behavior with mocks; `git diff --check` passed. No live database test was run.

units.first_call_model_response_cycle: One-based ordinal of unique rawResponse/completed responseId boundaries within the matching thread/turn; mapping uses a direct call ID or an explicitly labeled unique closed exec interval inference.
units.skillfetch_called: An observed model MCP invocation attempt, including calls blocked before server execution by approval policy.
units.successful_server_call: An observed completed MCP lifecycle with status completed, a non-null server result and no protocol-level failure; this does not assess task-result correctness.
units.outer_user_turn_index: One only when execution_started is true in the task manifest; independent of model response cycles.
units.action_ordinal: First-seen ordinal among distinct actionable item IDs in item/started or item/completed events.
units.item_ordinal: First-seen ordinal among all distinct item IDs in item/started or item/completed events.
units.stage4_comparison: Stage4 assistant-message counts are a different unit and are not directly equated to model-response cycles or outer user turns.

limitations: Counts describe observed skillfetch MCP lifecycle events, deduplicated by item.id; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence in incomplete transcripts.
Returned skill IDs come only from result.structuredContent.skills or JSON text result.content[].text skills arrays; requested IDs, resolver candidates and error IDs are excluded.
Legacy raw-event payloads and code-mode parent-call relationships are not inferred without an observed/schema-supported causal mapping.

const queries = ["Fix item and user update requests accepting null values for non-nullable fields while preserving nullable fields and public response models.","Add request-model validation and API regression tests to return HTTP 422 before database writes for explicit nulls.","Python SQLModel models in backend/app/models.py and item/user routes with tests in backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py and test_users.py; other stack details are unspecified.",'Bug: `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` returns a 500 instead of a validation error when the body sets `title` to null.
- Repro: create an item, then `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` with `{"title": null}`. `ItemUpdate` in `backend/app/models.py` accepts the null. `update_item` in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` then copies it onto the row through `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` and `sqlmodel_update`, and the commit fails on the non-null `title` column.
- Same pattern in `PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}`: `UserUpdate` allows `email`, `is_active` and `is_superuser` to be null. `update_user` only checks `if user_in.email:` and `crud.update_user` writes the nulls through.
- Explicit nulls on non-nullable fields must be rejected with a 422 before anything reaches the session.
- `description` (items) and `full_name` (users) must stay clearable by sending null. This is a product decision; don't change it.
- The `ItemPublic` and `UserPublic` response models must stay unchanged.
Acceptance: new cases in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py` and `backend/tests/api/routes/test_users.py` cover the null-title, null-email and cleared-description/full_name paths. All existing tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/` pass unchanged.'];

queries: Fix frontend API error handling so permission 403 responses show error toasts instead of logging users out.
Make a minimal change that logs out only on 401 or a 403 with detail Could not validate credentials, without new packages or generated client edits.

The known targets are TypeScript TSX frontend/src/main.tsx and frontend/src/components/UserSettings/DeleteConfirmation.tsx, with Python backend/app/api/deps.py providing authentication context; other stack details are unspecified.

In the frontend, any 403 from the API logs the user out. `handleApiError` in `frontend/src/main.tsx` clears `access_token` and redirects to `/login` for both 401 and 403. Ordinary permission errors therefore act like an expired session. One example is "Not enough permissions" from the items routes. Another is a superuser hitting Delete in `frontend/src/components/UserSettings/DeleteConfirmation.tsx`, which gets "Super users are not allowed to delete themselves". In both cases the user is kicked to the login page instead of seeing the error toast. The backend's real invalid-token case is the 403 with detail "Could not validate credentials" raised in `get_current_user` (`backend/app/api/deps.py`). Keep the diff minimal: only log out on 401 or on that specific credentials 403, and let every other 403 fall through to the existing `handleError` toast. Add no new packages, and don't touch the generated client in `frontend/src/client`.
